messages:
sanya: Heads-up: the OpenAPI for /v1/generate lists `model: 'gpt-lite'` as a valid enum in examples, but runtime only accepts `gpt-light` (note the dash). SDK snippets in the doc use the wrong value and fail validation in CI.
kevin: Ack. Do you have the failing log?
sanya: From preview CI:
```
Error: Invalid model value: 'gpt-lite' not in enum ['gpt-light','gpt-pro']
Usage: request rejected with 400
```
kevin: Oof. This is a classic docs generation vs. runtime enum drift. I'll open a PR to update OpenAPI examples and the snippet templates. Also we should add a short migration note mapping old display name -> API enum to avoid future churn.
docs-bot: PR created by kevin: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4907 
kevin: Changes in the PR: 1) replace `gpt-lite` with `gpt-light` in all OpenAPI examples, 2) update Python/JS snippet templates, 3) add a tiny section in the breaking-changes doc describing the enum rename and why it happened.
sanya: Please also update the JSON example in the Go quickstart — it still constructs the request using the incorrect string.
kevin: Will do. Also adding a short unit-test for the docs generator to validate example enums against the runtime schema file.
sdk-release-bot: Reminder: after merge, remember to bump docs-tag and regenerate SDKs.
sanya: I'll take Python SDK regen after merge and publish a patch if needed.
docs-bot: CI: docs-linter passed for PR #4907 
https://ci.redwood.ai/13299
kevin: Merged and preview updated: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/generate shows corrected enum and snippet.
sanya: Verified the preview and ran a quick local demo; validation passes now. Closing out.
